title: The cost of leaving convenience
lines: The assistant that makes your life easier may also make leaving its world harder.
Ecology of Predation uses a careful comparison with living systems to study how useful services can create dependence.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Keep the helpful household agent close to real daily tasks; remove any predator-as-villain animation.
voiceDirections: Speak with familiar unease; give gentle emphasis to leaving its world harder. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.

Speak with calm curiosity; lightly emphasize useful services can create dependence. Present this specific idea in a simple conversational voice, without a grand announcement or dramatic suspense, and leave a natural pause.

title: An ordinary assisted day
lines: An imagined household relies on an agent for contracts, purchases, family information, and daily coordination.
Each service helps, while the relationships around it can accumulate data, influence, and bargaining power.

title: Dependence in its environment
lines: The book uses careful comparisons with ecology to examine resources, adaptation, and the cost of leaving.
It follows connected pressures rather than imagining a simple chase between predator and prey.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Use the existing exit or portability objects to show continuity requirements, not a completed escape.
voiceDirections: Speak with thoughtful interest; give gentle emphasis to cost of leaving. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.
Speak with clear caution; give gentle emphasis to connected pressures. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.

title: What must leave with you?
lines: Small conveniences become more troubling when the same provider begins holding every key.
Begin in Mara’s household, and ask what would have to travel with her if she left.

emotionalPlan.purpose: End with Mara’s household and the things an export button cannot automatically carry.
voiceDirections: Speak with restrained unease; give gentle emphasis to holding every key. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.
